correctness.rationale: The proof gives an exact unit-step reduction by Stieltjes mixtures and convexity, then a least-favorable uniform central jump prior yields an L² square-completion lower bound. The candidate clips local u−1/2 at 1/(2n); its conditional step-risk derivative is positive, zero, and negative on the three intervals, making the lower bound tight and establishing uniqueness. All normalization factors and equality cases are explicit. A standalone rational checker executed 3,217 passing assertions; the proof does not rely on finite checks.

value.rationale: The universal bounded-monotone integration problem naturally requires a preselected variance reducer when integrands may jump and evaluation is costly. The result closes an infinite-dimensional minimax optimization over all separate stratumwise controls, giving a unique nonlinear rule and exact finite-n gains: for n=2, 7/192 versus 1/16 uncontrolled (5/12 relative reduction), and below the unstratified two-point CV benchmark 1/24. The asymptotic n^−2 rate remains unchanged, and no downstream theorem or unrestricted estimator optimality is claimed.
